paper.title: Meta-Learning Hypothesis Spaces for Sequential Decision-making

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian optimization / kernelized bandit with unknown kernel meta-learned from offline data
unmapped: True kernel k* is unknown; it is a sparse nonnegative combination of p known finite-dimensional base kernels
Learner has offline meta-data from m tasks with n samples each, from the same RKHS
Learner knows a bound B on the RKHS norm of f under the true kernel
Group beta-min condition (Assumption 3.1) and restricted eigenvalue condition (Assumption 4.2) on the meta-data
Domain X is a compact subset of R^{d_0}
settings.definition_quote: Consider a sequential decision-making problem, where the agent repeatedly interacts with an environment and makes observations y_t = f(x_t) + \varepsilon_t of an unknown function f residing in an RKHS H_{k^*} that corresponds to an unknown kernel function k^*. We further assume that the function has a bounded kernel norm \norm{f}_{k^*} \leq B and that the domain X is compact. The observation noise are i.i.d. samples from a zero-mean sub-Gaussian distribution with variance proxy \sigma^2.

bound.expression_latex: R_T= \gO\Bigg( \sqrt{\hat d T\log T}  \Big( B\big(1 + \epsilon(n,m)\big) + \sqrt{\hat d \log T+ \log1/\delta}\Big)\Bigg)

symbols.d_hat: sum of feature dimensions d_j of base kernels active in the meta-learned kernel
symbols.B_rkhs: bound on the RKHS norm of f under the true kernel
symbols.eps_nm: epsilon(n,m) = 32 sigma s/(kappa^2 sqrt(mn)) * sqrt(1 + (2/m)(log(2p/delta) + sqrt(m d_max log(2p/delta)))), meta-learning error

conditions: f in RKHS of unknown k* with ||f||_{k*} <= B
k* is a sparse combination of p known finite-dimensional base kernels with |J_k*| <= s
Assumption 3.1 (group beta-min with c_1) and Assumption 4.2 (restricted eigenvalue kappa(s)) hold
n, m large enough that epsilon(n,m) <= c_1
tuning: nu_t = B(1 + eps(n,m)/(2c_1)) + sigma*sqrt(d_hat*log(1 + bar_sigma^{-2} t/c_1) + 2 + 2 log(1/delta))

source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Suppose $f\in \tH$ with $\norm{f}_\tk \leq B$ and that values of $f$ are observed with zero-mean sub-Gaussian noise of variance proxy $\sigma^2$. Then, with probability greater than $1-\delta$, \textsc{GP-UCB} used together with $\khat$ satisfies R_T= O( \sqrt{\hat d T\log T} ( B(1 + \epsilon(n,m)) + \sqrt{\hat d \log T+ \log1/\delta})) provided that the exploration coefficient is set to ...

results.notes: Regret defined as sum f(x*) - f(x_t), bounded with high probability. Probability covers both meta-learning recovery and online confidence. Horizon: nu_t does not depend on T, so treated as anytime. Theorem 4.3, Prop 4.4 and Theorem 5.1 (hypothesis recovery, sparsity, confidence bounds) are not regret guarantees and were not recorded.
